Gentianaceae.key_door: opposite exstipulate leaves + fused corolla + superior many-ovuled ovary + many-seeded capsule

Loganiaceae.key_door: opposite leaves + stipule/interpetiolar-line clues + superior usually 2-locular ovary + distinctive capsules

Gelsemiaceae.key_door: woody twining yellow jessamine + 4-segment septicidal capsule + unilaterally winged seeds

lineage_lesson: Gentianales repeatedly uses opposite leaves and fused corollas. Split the local families by stipules, ovary position, fruit/seed architecture, latex, and growth habit rather than flower shape alone.
taxonomy_notes: Centaurium beyrichii, C. calycosum and C. texense are retained as source-name provenance but taught under current Zeltnera concepts.
Centaurium tenuiflorum remains accepted in Centaurium and is treated separately from the Zeltnera remaps.
Eustoma exaltatum subsp. russellianum is reconciled to Eustoma russellianum; E. exaltatum remains a separate accepted species.
Older broad Loganiaceae treatments may include Gelsemium; the current learner places it in Gelsemiaceae.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Preserve historical/source names as provenance rather than creating duplicate current taxa.
Use Apocynaceae and Rubiaceae as comparison anchors; do not rebuild their family lessons in this batch.
